# Adjudication Task — Chapter 371

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃371화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“열화신룡(烈火神龍) 진태경 대협을 뵙습니다!”
  6|
  7|경외를 담은 외침이 사천당문의 경내에 울려 퍼진 그 순간, 전율을 느낀 것은 진태경 한 사람뿐만이 아니었다.
  8|
  9|멀리서 모든 광경을 지켜보던 늙은 스승은 벅차오르는 감정을 숨기기 위해 안간힘을 써야 했다.
 10|
 11|‘녀석…….’
 12|
 13|적천강은 진태경을 처음 만난 날을 또렷이 기억하고 있었다.
 14|
 15|변방 무가의 삼공자. 이제 갓 산서 땅에서 이름을 알리기 시작했던 어린 청년은 잠룡이 되었고, 마침내 날개를 활짝 펴고 푸른 하늘로 비상하고 있었다.
 16|
 17|‘그래, 네 녀석이야말로 신룡(神龍)이요, 대협(大俠)이다.’
 18|
 19|눈이 마주치자 씩 웃는 진태경의 얼굴이 보인다. 창밖으로 상반신을 내민 그가 두 손을 미친 듯이 휘저었다.
 20|
 21|“내 이름이 뭐라고?”
 22|
 23|“진태경!”
 24|
 25|“별호는 뭐라고!”
 26|
 27|“열화신룡!”
 28|
 29|“더 크게 소리 질러-!”
 30|
 31|“와아아아아!”
 32|
 33|엄숙하던 장내가 한 번에 뒤집어지며 광란의 도가니로 변하는 광경에, 적천강은 참았던 웃음을 터트렸다.
 34|
 35|“으하, 으하하하!”
 36|
 37|시원한 웃음소리와 함성이 뒤섞인다. 바람은 시원했고 하늘은 맑았다.
 38|
 39|바야흐로 난세(亂世)의 시작이었으나, 새로운 영웅이 태동하던 그 날은 따스한 봄이었다.
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|* * *
 44|
 45|
 46|
 47|적천강이 나타난 것은 광란의 도가니가 가라앉은 직후였다.
 48|
 49|“좁쌀만 한 방에 많이도 모여 있구나.”
 50|
 51|“어? 하나도 안 좁은데요?”
 52|
 53|“적 대협, 저쪽에 빈자리가 있습니다.”
 54|
 55|눈치라고는 죽었다가 깨어나도 없는 청풍이나 혁무진과는 달리, 뼛속까지 성골 거지인 궁기방은 즉각 움직였다.
 56|
 57|“어이구, 그러고 보니까 좁아서 미어터질 것 같네요. 저는 나가 있겠습니다.”
 58|
 59|청풍과 혁무진이 손을 흔들어 주었다.
 60|
 61|“잘 가요, 궁 소협.”
 62|
 63|“저 양반 드디어 가네. 조장, 아까부터 어디서 똥개 궁둥이 냄새 나지 않았습니까?”
 64|
 65|나는 조심스럽게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 66|
 67|“어, 조금 심하게 나긴 하더라…….”
 68|
 69|“개소리 그만하고 둘 다 나와!”
 70|
 71|“아니, 진짜 났다니까…….”
 72|
 73|“알겠어요. 그렇게 화내지 마세요, 궁 소협.”
 74|
 75|벌컥 성을 내는 궁기방의 모습에 청풍이 시무룩한 얼굴로 고개를 숙였다.
 76|
 77|“미미. 회오리 치기 하면서 인사.”
 78|
 79|취릭. 취리리릭!
 80|
 81|“……뭐여, 시벌.”
 82|
 83|그사이 스킬이 늘었네. 화려한 퍼포먼스를 보여 준 청풍이 마지막으로 방을 나서자 적천강이 입을 열었다.
 84|
 85|“천둥벌거숭이 같으니. 아주 한바탕 난리를 치더구나.”
 86|
 87|굳은 얼굴과 착 가라앉은 목소리. 참 여전하다. 평소의 적천강 같아서 왠지 웃음이 나왔다.
 88|
 89|“웃어?”
 90|
 91|“그럼 웃지, 웁니까?”
 92|
 93|“허, 이놈 보게나. 사람들 앞에서 추태를 부려 본문의 명성에 먹칠을 해 놓고도 그런 말이 나오느냐?”
 94|
 95|“그렇게 생각하신 것치고는 엄청 크게 웃으시던데.”
 96|
 97|“……!”
 98|
 99|“다 봤어요.”
100|
101|애써 유지하던 굳은 표정이 와르르 무너졌다. 적천강의 고개가 슬그머니 창밖을 향해 돌아갔다.
102|
103|“크흠. 보긴 뭘 봤단 말이더냐.”
104|
105|“저 말고도 오십 명쯤은 봤을걸요. 입꼬리에서 피 나시는 줄.”
106|
107|거의 차이나 조커 수준이었지.
108|
109|도무지 빠져나올 틈을 주지 않는 내 확인 사살에, 한참이나 머뭇거리며 말을 잇지 못하던 적천강이 한마디를 툭 내뱉었다.
110|
111|“……했다.”
112|
113|“예?”
114|
115|“아, 잘했다고!”
116|
117|벌겋게 달아오른 얼굴로 외친 적천강이 작게 툴툴거린다.
118|
119|그 모습에 내 입가에 맺힌 웃음이 더욱 짙어졌다. 그래, 그 한마디면 충분하다.
120|
121|“감사합니다. 전부 노야 덕분이에요.”
122|
123|“…….”
124|
125|뭐지? 어째 표정이 심상치 않다.
126|
127|섭섭함마저 느껴지는 눈빛에 황당해진 내가 물었다.
128|
129|“이번엔 또 왜요?”
130|
131|“아니다. 아무것도.”
132|
133|“그런 것치곤 표정이 어째 좀…….”
134|
135|“아니라니까!”
136|
137|“아니, 왜 소리를 지르고 그러세요? 오랜만에 분위기 훈훈하고 좋았는데.”
138|
139|“거, 아니라면 아닌 줄 알 것이지. 네 녀석이 자꾸 꼬치꼬치 캐물으니까 이러는 것 아니냐!”
140|
141|“어어, 점점?”
142|
143|이 양반 갑자기 왜 이래. 내가 무슨 실수라도 했나?
144|
145|어리둥절해서 고개를 갸웃거리던 그때였다.
146|
147|스슥.
148|
149|계단을 올라오는 두 개의 인기척.
150|
151|벽을 넘어서며 한층 더 예민해진 감각이 아니었다면 쉽게 알아차리지 못했을 만큼, 그들의 걸음은 가볍고 표횰했다.
152|
153|‘둘 다 엄청난 고수들이다.’
154|
155|갑자기 초절정의 고수가 둘씩이나?
156|
157|최근 들어 많은 위기를 겪은 탓에 이제는 몸이 저절로 움직였다.
158|
159|그런데 적천강이 주먹을 말아쥐는 나를 눈짓으로 만류하더니 손을 내저었다. 한 줄기의 열풍이 닫혀 있던 문을 부드럽게 열어젖혔다.
160|
161|“다들 성질도 급하군. 일각도 못 기다리고 우르르 몰려와?”
162|
163|적천강의 불퉁한 목소리에 늙은 여승과 도사가 차례대로 대답했다.
164|
165|“성질이 급하다니. 시주에게 들으니 기분이 참 묘해지는구려.”
166|
167|“후배가 결례를 저질렀습니다. 다만 사안이 사안인지라.”
168|
169|쪼글쪼글한 주름이 가득한 늙은 여승은 초면이었지만, 도사가 누군지는 금방 알아볼 수 있었다.
170|
171|나는 노고사를 향해 포권을 취했다.
172|
173|“안녕하십니까. 진인(眞人).”
174|
175|“다시 보니 반갑네. 진 도우.”
176|
177|노도사의 정체는 일전에 신의를 찾기 위해 도움을 청하러 간 청성파의 장문인인 청풍고검(淸風高劍)이었다.
178|
179|‘그럼 이 여승이 아미파의 장문인일 텐데…… 누구지?’
180|
181|나도 이제 무림 짬밥이 좀 되다 보니 유명한 고수에 관한 것들은 어느 정도 알고 있는데, 남의 문파 사정까지 속속들이 꿰고 있을 정도는 아니었다.
182|
183|경천신니의 죽음 이후 새로 취임한 장문인의 경우에는 더더욱.
184|
185|내 생각을 읽은 듯, 적천강이 넌지시 전음을 보냈다.
186|
187|- 그 할망구는 아미파의 멸절신니(滅絶神尼)다. 보기에는 인자해 보여도 한 번 눈이 뒤집히면 나찰이 따로 없으니 언행에 특별히 신경 써라. 특히 나이에 관해서는 입도 벙긋하지 말고.
188|
189|나도 조심스럽게 전음으로 응수했다.
190|
191|- 춘추가 어떻게 되시길래.
192|
193|- 노부보다 많다. 경천신니의 사고이기도 하지.
194|
195|- 아.
196|
197|적천강의 정확한 나이는 모르지만, 백 세를 넘겼다는 것만은 안다. 거기에 더해 별호에서 느껴지는 포스까지.
198|
199|나는 보쌈집 회장님 같아 보이는 왕 할머니에게 넙죽 허리를 숙였다.
200|
201|“안녕하십니까! 진태경이라고 합니다!”
202|
203|“반갑네, 진 시주.”
204|
205|묘한 눈빛으로 나를 응시하던 멸절신니가 고개를 끄덕였다.
206|
207|“소문대로군. 아니, 그 이상이야.”
208|
209|청풍고검이 희미하게 웃으며 말을 받았다.
210|
211|“실로 놀랍지 않습니까.”
212|
213|“장강후랑추전랑(長江後浪推前浪). 장강의 뒷물결이 이 늙은이들까지 밀어내려 하는구려. 이토록 어린 나이에 벽을 넘어서다니…….”
214|
215|“그뿐만이 아닙니다, 신니. 청풍이라는 젊은이도 있지요.”
216|
217|“아, 그 검성의 후인이라는?”
218|
219|“예. 빈도가 부족한 탓에 우열을 가릴 수는 없겠으나, 두 젊은이 모두 하늘이 내린 인물들이 확실합니다. 무림의 큰 흥복이지요.”
220|
221|“호오…….”
222|
223|피곤함이 묻어나던 두 사람의 얼굴 위로 흥미와 놀라움이 스친다.
224|
225|어쩐지 민망해져서 눈동자만 굴리고 있던 그때, 적천강이 내 앞을 슥 가로막았다.
226|
227|그래 봤자 키 차이가 워낙 나서 달라질 것도 없었지만.
228|
229|“애 얼굴 닳겠소. 할 말이나 후딱 하고 가.”
230|
231|퉁명스러운 말에 머쓱해진 두 장문인이 본론을 꺼내 들었다.
232|
233|“문제가 생겼네. 두 사람 모두 잠시 동행해 줄 수 있겠나?”
234|
235|“오래 걸리지 않을 겁니다. 약속드리지요.”
236|
237|“동행? 지금 당장?”
238|
239|탐탁지 않은 목소리로 되물은 적천강이 돌아서며 내게 물었다.
240|
241|“어찌하겠느냐?”
242|
243|“…….”
244|
245|구파일방의 두 장문인이 부탁하는데 나보고 뭘 어쩌라고.
246|
247|“가겠습니다.”
248|
249|어차피 몸도 가뿐하겠다, 동행하면서 지금까지의 전후 사정을 들을 수 있을 테니 딱히 거절할 이유가 없었다.
250|
251|내 흔쾌한 대답에 두 장문인이 앞장서서 걸음을 떼는데, 적천강이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
252|
253|“그런데, 한 놈은 왜 안 보여?”
254|
255|“아래에서 기다리고 있다네.”
256|
257|“다른 사람들 눈에 띄기 싫다 하시더군요.”
258|
259|한 놈? 이 멤버에 낄 정도면 당문의 가주인 당사독인가?
260|
261|‘뭐, 누구건 곧 보게 되겠지.’
262|
263|하지만 내 궁금증은 전각을 나서자마자 마주친 한 사람에 의해 씻은 듯이 사라졌다.
264|
265|낯익은 얼굴을 보자 절로 반가움이 담긴 외침이 터져 나왔다.
266|
267|“야, 인마! 문경!”
268|
269|문경은 사천당문을 떠나기 전의 모습 그대로였다.
270|
271|안 그래도 녀석이 떠난 지 얼마 되지 않아 암천이 쳐들어온 탓에 걱정이 들었는데, 길이 엇갈렸는지 용케도 다치지 않았다.
272|
273|“언제부터 와 있었어? 이 자식 이거, 못 본 사이에 키가 더 커진 것 같네. 요즘 성장기냐?”
274|
275|“…….”
276|
277|“왜 이렇게 말이 없어. 기분 안 좋아? 혹시…….”
278|
279|문경의 머리를 쓱쓱 헤집던 나는 숨죽여 속삭였다.
280|
281|“아침에 몽정했냐?”
282|
283|“……!”
284|
285|“했네. 했어.”
286|
287|짜식, 부끄러워서 아무 말도 안 하는 것 봐라.
288|
289|나는 흐뭇하게 웃었다.
290|
291|원래 저 나이대에는 종종 있는 일이다. 이참에 이 케케묵은 무림에 올바른 성 지식을 전파하는 것도 좋겠지.
292|
293|“이 형님이 신세계를 알려 주마. 앞으로 진성애 선생님이라고 불러라.”
294|
295|구성애 선생님. 보고 계십니까. 당신의 지식이 시공을 넘어 전해지고 있습니다.
296|
297|뿌듯한 감정을 느끼며 문경의 어깨를 탁탁 두드리던 그 순간이었다.
298|
299|“어…….”
300|
301|“그…….”
302|
303|“허어…… 저걸 말 안 해 줬네.”
304|
305|말 안 해 주다니. 뭘?
306|
307|등 뒤에서 들려오는 세 사람의 장탄식. 동시에 문경의 입술 사이로 무미건조한 음성이 흘러나왔다.
308|
309|“손. 치워라.”
310|
311|“……어?”
312|
313|“그리고 몽정은 오래전에 끝났다.”
314|
315|“그건 좀 문제가 있는데, 왜냐하면 네가 아직 이차 성징이 완전히 안 끝났……이 아니라.”
316|
317|나는 침을 꼴깍 삼켰다.
318|
319|문득, 어떤 무서운 상상이 뇌리를 스쳤기 때문이었다.
320|
321|“누구……세요?”
322|
323|엄마, 나 무서워.
324|
325|
326|
327|* * *
328|
329|
330|
331|“……해서, 이렇게 된 걸세.”
332|
333|“참으로 해괴한 일이지.”
334|

Yes. That one sentence was enough.

[P61]
“Thank you. It was all thanks to you, Old Master.”

[P62]
“…”

[P63]
What was this? His expression had suddenly turned strange.

[P64]
He almost looked hurt. Baffled, I asked,

[P65]
“What’s wrong this time?”

[P66]
“Nothing. It’s nothing.”

[P67]
“Your face doesn’t exactly say nothing…”

[P68]
“I said it was nothing!”

[P69]
“Why are you shouting? Things were finally warm and pleasant for once.”

[P70]
“If I say it’s nothing, then take it as nothing! You’re the one who keeps prying!”

[P71]
“Whoa. It’s getting worse?”

[P72]
What was wrong with this man all of a sudden? Had I screwed something up?

[P73]
I was tilting my head in confusion when—

[P74]
Rustle.

[P75]
Two presences were coming up the stairs.

[P76]
Their footsteps were so light and graceful that I might never have noticed them if my senses hadn’t grown even sharper after crossing the threshold.

[P77]
*They’re both incredible masters.*

[P78]
Two Supreme Peak masters, just like that?

[P79]
After all the crises I had weathered lately, my body moved on its own.

[P80]
But as I clenched my fists, Jeok Cheongang stopped me with a glance and waved one hand.

[P81]
A thin stream of hot air gently pushed open the closed door.

[P82]
“You’re all so impatient. Couldn’t even wait fifteen minutes before swarming up here?”

[P83]
An elderly Buddhist nun and a Daoist answered Jeok Cheongang’s gruff complaint in turn.

[P84]
“To hear you call someone else impatient feels rather strange.”

[P85]
“This junior has been discourteous. However, given the circumstances…”

[P86]
The elderly nun, her face covered in fine wrinkles, was a stranger to me. But I immediately recognized the Daoist.

[P87]
I cupped my hands toward him.

[P88]
“Greetings, Perfected One.”

[P89]
“It’s good to see you again, Fellow Daoist Jin.”

[P90]
The old Daoist was Cheongpung the Ancient Sword, the Sect Leader of the Qingcheng Sect whom I had once visited to ask for help finding the Divine Physician.

[P91]
*Then this nun must be Emei Sect’s new Sect Leader… Who is she?*

[P92]
I knew a fair amount about famous masters by now, but not enough to understand the inner workings of every sect.

[P93]
Especially when it came to a Sect Leader who had only recently taken office after the death of the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.

[P94]
As if he had read my thoughts, Jeok Cheongang quietly sent me a Sound Transmission.

[P95]
*That old hag is Emei Sect’s Extinction Divine Nun. She may look kindly, but once she loses her temper, she becomes a rakshasa incarnate. Watch your mouth around her. And whatever you do, don’t mention her age.*

[P96]
I cautiously sent one back.

[P97]
*Just how old is she?*

[P98]
*Older than this old man. She was also the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun’s Senior Aunt.*

[P99]
*Oh.*

[P100]
I didn’t know Jeok Cheongang’s exact age, but I knew he was over a hundred. Add the sheer force of that sobriquet…

[P101]
I bowed deeply to the ancient woman who looked like the matriarch of a bossam restaurant.[^1]

[P102]
“Greetings! My name is Jin Taekyung!”

[P103]
“Good to meet you, Benefactor Jin.”

[P104]
The Extinction Divine Nun studied me with an inscrutable look, then nodded.

[P105]
“So the rumors were true. No—they fell short.”

[P106]
Cheongpung the Ancient Sword smiled faintly.

[P107]
“Isn’t it truly astonishing?”

[P108]
“The waves behind drive the waves ahead on the Yangtze. It seems the younger generation means to sweep even old people like us aside. To cross the threshold at such a young age…”

[P109]
“It isn’t only him, Venerable Nun. There is also a young man named Cheongpung.”

[P110]
“Ah, the Sword Saint’s successor?”

[P111]
“Yes. This poor Daoist lacks the discernment to judge which of the two is superior, but both young men are unquestionably heaven-sent. They are a great blessing to the Murim.”

[P112]
“Oh…”

[P113]
Interest and surprise flickered across their weary faces.

[P114]
I was shifting my eyes awkwardly when Jeok Cheongang stepped in front of me.

[P115]
Not that it accomplished much, considering the difference in our heights.

[P116]
“You’ll wear the boy’s face out staring at him. Say what you came to say and hurry along.”

[P117]
Chastened by his blunt words, the two Sect Leaders finally got to the point.

[P118]
“A problem has arisen. Could the two of you accompany us for a while?”

[P119]
“It won’t take long. You have my word.”

[P120]
“Accompany you? Right now?”

[P121]
Jeok Cheongang asked in a displeased voice, then turned to me.

[P122]
“What will you do?”

[P123]
“…”

[P124]
Two Sect Leaders from the Nine Sects and One Gang were asking for my help. What was I supposed to say?

[P125]
“I’ll go.”

[P126]
My body felt light, and accompanying them would give me a chance to hear everything that had happened. There was no real reason to refuse.

[P127]
At my ready answer, the two Sect Leaders took the lead.

[P128]
Then Jeok Cheongang abruptly asked,

[P129]
“But where’s the other one?”

[P130]
“He’s waiting below.”

[P131]
“He said he preferred not to attract anyone else’s attention.”

[P132]
The other one? If he was important enough to join this group, was it Tang Sadok, the Family Head of the Tang Clan?

[P133]
*Well, whoever it is, I’ll see him soon enough.*

[P134]
But my curiosity vanished the moment we left the pavilion and encountered a familiar face.

[P135]
A delighted shout burst from me.

[P136]
“Hey, you little punk! Mungyeong!”

[P137]
Mungyeong looked exactly as he had before leaving the Sichuan Tang Clan.

[P138]
Dark Heaven had attacked not long after his departure, so I’d been worried about him. But perhaps our paths had simply crossed, because he had somehow escaped without a scratch.

[P139]
“When did you get here? You look taller than before. Going through a growth spurt?”

[P140]
“…”

[P141]
“Why so quiet? Are you in a bad mood? Maybe…”

[P142]
I ruffled Mungyeong’s hair, then leaned closer and whispered,

[P143]
“Did you have a wet dream this morning?”

[P144]
“…!”

[P145]
“You did. You totally did.”

[P146]
Look at the little brat. Too embarrassed to say a word.

[P147]
I smiled with satisfaction.

[P148]
That sort of thing happened from time to time at his age. Maybe this was my chance to spread proper sex education throughout this dusty old Murim.

[P149]
“Your hyung is going to show you a whole new world. From now on, call me Teacher Jin Seong-ae.”[^2]

[P150]
Teacher Gu Seong-ae, are you watching? Your wisdom is crossing space and time to reach the next generation.

[P151]
I was proudly patting Mungyeong on the shoulder when—

[P152]
“Uh…”

[P153]
“Um…”

[P154]
“Oh dear… We forgot to tell him.”

[P155]
Forgot to tell me what?

[P156]
Three long sighs sounded behind me. At the same time, Mungyeong spoke in a flat voice.

[P157]
“Take your hand off.”

[P158]
“…Huh?”

[P159]
“And I stopped having wet dreams a long time ago.”

[P160]
“That’s a little concerning, because your secondary sexual development shouldn’t be complete y—wait. That’s not the point.”

[P161]
I swallowed hard.

[P162]
A terrifying possibility had just flashed through my mind.

[P163]
“Who… are you?”

[P164]
Mom, I’m scared.

[P165]
* * *

[P166]
“…And that is how things came to this.”

[P167]
“It truly is a bizarre matter.”

[P168]
Even as the two Sect Leaders raced along using their movement techniques, their voices never wavered.

[P169]
They looked at me, waiting for an answer. I forced my lips apart.

[P170]
“Ah, right. So there’s some kind of strange formation where we’re going?”

[P171]
“That is what we learned after capturing and interrogating the Third Fiend. But the formation itself is so peculiar…”

[P172]
Jeok Cheongang answered gruffly.

[P173]
“This old man and this brat are both hopeless when it comes to formations. Looking at it won’t tell us a damned thing.”

[P174]
I agreed. The Fire Gate Cavern on Mount Jiuhua contained an extraordinary Mystic Gate Formation, but that didn’t make either of us experts.

[P175]
*We’d be better off calling someone from the Zhuge Clan.*

[P176]
But it would take the Zhuge Clan a considerable amount of time to get here.

[P177]
For some reason, the two Sect Leaders seemed to have high expectations of us.

[P178]
Especially me.

[P179]
“Fellow Daoist Jin, did you notice anything else strange about that man? Anything in his words or behavior?”

[P180]
“I’ve told you everything. And from what I could tell… I don’t think it was possible for him to get any stranger.”

[P181]
Dark Heaven was inherently strange. They were fanatics who worshiped the Lord of Heaven almost—no, exactly—like a god.

[P182]
The Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord were no different, with all their bizarre powers and abilities.

[P183]
*One regenerated like a human Troll. Another popped his arm off and stuck it back on like he had double-sided tape under it. And then there was the possession at the end.*

[P184]
The more I thought about it, the more miraculous our victory seemed.

[P185]
We had fought those lunatics and somehow won.

[P186]
“Before you awoke, Benefactor Jeok gave us a general account of what happened. Once the messenger eagle we sent to Henan returns with a reply, we should have a clearer idea of how to proceed.”

[P187]
“If you notice anything strange when you examine the formation, tell us.”

[P188]
“Yes.”

[P189]
As I answered, I glanced at the figure racing far ahead of us.

[P190]
Mungyeong.

[P191]
No—the man known as the Slaughter Saint.

[P192]
*Fuck. What the hell is the Slaughter Saint doing here?*

[P193]
Honestly, I had nearly pissed myself.

[P194]
Even if I’d spent half a day frolicking in the Sanzu River and stopped to grill some meat before coming back, I couldn’t have come any closer to death.[^3]

[P195]
*Mungyeong was the Slaughter Saint. And I asked the Slaughter Saint if he’d had a wet dream!*

[P196]
Teacher Gu Seong-ae, I nearly died because of you.

[P197]
I had just let out a private sigh of relief when the dense undergrowth around us fell away, revealing towering cliffs ahead.

[P198]
[^1]: Bossam is boiled pork commonly wrapped in salted napa cabbage and served with condiments; a bossam restaurant matriarch evokes the familiar image of an elderly Korean neighborhood restaurateur.

[P199]
[^2]: Gu Seong-ae is a Korean sex educator. Taekyung parodies her name by replacing Gu with Jin.

[P200]
[^3]: In Buddhist tradition, the Sanzu River marks the boundary between life and death.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",

},

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 371

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃371화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“열화신룡(烈火神龍) 진태경 대협을 뵙습니다!”
  6|
  7|경외를 담은 외침이 사천당문의 경내에 울려 퍼진 그 순간, 전율을 느낀 것은 진태경 한 사람뿐만이 아니었다.
  8|
  9|멀리서 모든 광경을 지켜보던 늙은 스승은 벅차오르는 감정을 숨기기 위해 안간힘을 써야 했다.
 10|
 11|‘녀석…….’
 12|
 13|적천강은 진태경을 처음 만난 날을 또렷이 기억하고 있었다.
 14|
 15|변방 무가의 삼공자. 이제 갓 산서 땅에서 이름을 알리기 시작했던 어린 청년은 잠룡이 되었고, 마침내 날개를 활짝 펴고 푸른 하늘로 비상하고 있었다.
 16|
 17|‘그래, 네 녀석이야말로 신룡(神龍)이요, 대협(大俠)이다.’
 18|
 19|눈이 마주치자 씩 웃는 진태경의 얼굴이 보인다. 창밖으로 상반신을 내민 그가 두 손을 미친 듯이 휘저었다.
 20|
 21|“내 이름이 뭐라고?”
 22|
 23|“진태경!”
 24|
 25|“별호는 뭐라고!”
 26|
 27|“열화신룡!”
 28|
 29|“더 크게 소리 질러-!”
 30|
 31|“와아아아아!”
 32|
 33|엄숙하던 장내가 한 번에 뒤집어지며 광란의 도가니로 변하는 광경에, 적천강은 참았던 웃음을 터트렸다.
 34|
 35|“으하, 으하하하!”
 36|
 37|시원한 웃음소리와 함성이 뒤섞인다. 바람은 시원했고 하늘은 맑았다.
 38|
 39|바야흐로 난세(亂世)의 시작이었으나, 새로운 영웅이 태동하던 그 날은 따스한 봄이었다.
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|* * *
 44|
 45|
 46|
 47|적천강이 나타난 것은 광란의 도가니가 가라앉은 직후였다.
 48|
 49|“좁쌀만 한 방에 많이도 모여 있구나.”
 50|
 51|“어? 하나도 안 좁은데요?”
 52|
 53|“적 대협, 저쪽에 빈자리가 있습니다.”
 54|
 55|눈치라고는 죽었다가 깨어나도 없는 청풍이나 혁무진과는 달리, 뼛속까지 성골 거지인 궁기방은 즉각 움직였다.
 56|
 57|“어이구, 그러고 보니까 좁아서 미어터질 것 같네요. 저는 나가 있겠습니다.”
 58|
 59|청풍과 혁무진이 손을 흔들어 주었다.
 60|
 61|“잘 가요, 궁 소협.”
 62|
 63|“저 양반 드디어 가네. 조장, 아까부터 어디서 똥개 궁둥이 냄새 나지 않았습니까?”
 64|
 65|나는 조심스럽게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 66|
 67|“어, 조금 심하게 나긴 하더라…….”
 68|
 69|“개소리 그만하고 둘 다 나와!”
 70|
 71|“아니, 진짜 났다니까…….”
 72|
 73|“알겠어요. 그렇게 화내지 마세요, 궁 소협.”
 74|
 75|벌컥 성을 내는 궁기방의 모습에 청풍이 시무룩한 얼굴로 고개를 숙였다.
 76|
 77|“미미. 회오리 치기 하면서 인사.”
 78|
 79|취릭. 취리리릭!
 80|
 81|“……뭐여, 시벌.”
 82|
 83|그사이 스킬이 늘었네. 화려한 퍼포먼스를 보여 준 청풍이 마지막으로 방을 나서자 적천강이 입을 열었다.
 84|
 85|“천둥벌거숭이 같으니. 아주 한바탕 난리를 치더구나.”
 86|
 87|굳은 얼굴과 착 가라앉은 목소리. 참 여전하다. 평소의 적천강 같아서 왠지 웃음이 나왔다.
 88|
 89|“웃어?”
 90|
 91|“그럼 웃지, 웁니까?”
 92|

[P162]

[P168]

[P170]

[P171]

[P172]

[P173]

[P175]
*We’d be better off calling someone from the Zhuge Clan.*

[P176]

[P177]

[P178]

[P179]

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
